title: The Engineers' Confession
subtitle: The school asks the question the scholars keep dressing up: did you make us?

customObject.name: the seed vault
customObject.description: a squat case of grey ice-glass, older than the factions' arrival — inside, dim rows of seeds from a world nobody engineered, kept as evidence

script.note: The plaza, mid-morning. The Story is holding its open session on the question the scholars keep dressing in careful words. The schools were invited, which the factions did not expect. The front row is nine years old, and it has been waiting with its hand up since before the session opened.

script.text: For the Story, session forty: the origins question. The Council has agreed to answer under honest-memory rules — receipts, not comfort. And the keeper rules that the schools ask first, because the scholars ask in paragraphs and we'd be here till the solstice. Pia. You've had your hand up for eleven minutes. Go.
Did you make us? Everyone argues about it at lunch. Bruno says you built the first people like robots and that's why his uncle can wiggle his ears. Just — did you?

No. And I have brought the receipt, because your keeper warned me a plain no would not survive this plaza. That case, Pia — look at it, all of you. It is our oldest holding, older than our arrival here. It is full of seeds. We took them from this world's soil in our first century, when we understood no part of what we had found. Every one of them predates us. The grass, the grain, the thing that became the olive. And what the seeds carry — the growing, the reaching, the stubbornness — predates us by so far that our instruments give up counting. When my people landed, this world was already burning with life, top to bottom. We did not light one cell of it.
But you did SOMETHING. Or you wouldn't have called this the confession session. You don't confess nothing.
For the record: the child has just out-lawyered four thousand years of theology. Answer her, Sel. The middle part. The part your broadcasts keep flying over.

The middle part. Yes. We gardened, Pia. For thousands of years, without asking. We crossed your grains to feed more of you — that one I would do again. We nudged your settlements to the rivers we preferred. We taught the clever families and neglected the slow ones, and chose which was which by measures that flattered us. We adjusted the soil of your world, and sometimes — I will say it plainly, once, so the Story holds it — sometimes the seed. Small things. Sturdier backs. Sharper fevers, to burn sickness faster. We told ourselves it was tending. Looking down the centuries at what we chose and what we skipped, there are choices I would crawl the length of this world to unmake.

So Bruno's HALF right. You changed people. But — the alive part. The part that's ME, the me-that's-in-here part. Did you make THAT? Because that's the actual question, and grown-ups keep answering the seed one instead.

There it is. Six thousand years, and a nine-year-old walks the whole Council to the real door. No, Pia. The me-that's-in-here — the burning, the caring, the thing that looks out — we did not make it, we cannot make it, and we have tried. Oh, we have tried, in ways I will tell you about when you are older and can laugh at us properly. We found the flame already lit — in you, and if I am honest past my mandate, in everything, banked and waiting. All we ever did, at our very best, was cup our hands around it. And at our worst, for whole ages... we stood where the light fell, and let your people thank US for it.
Okay. So who made the fire?

We don't know. Upstream of us, upstream of everything we can instrument — something made it possible for matter to care. That is the true and complete answer, and my people have been asking it for longer than your species has had language: we don't know.

No. It's the address of one. The First Faction went up that road six thousand years ago, and the whole sky is still holding its breath for the postcard. When it comes, Pia, I suspect the schools will hear it before the scholars do. You people ask in the right direction.

Then let's close the record properly. Session forty, the origins question, findings as follows. One: they did not make us. Two: they meddled, extensively, and the meddling is confessed and filed, and the town will chew on it for a generation, as it should. Three — and I'll enter the child's own verdict here, because it's the cleanest summary this keeper has ever filed — Pia. Sum it up for the Story. What did we learn today?

'They don't know either.' Filed. And I want it noted that the plaza just breathed OUT, all together — six thousand years of wondering whether the sky was hiding the answer from us, and it turns out the sky is standing in the same queue, a bit further up, holding better instruments and the same face we make. Most reassuring finding the Story has ever published. Session closed. Bruno — see me about the ears; that one, I'm afraid, is all your uncle.

script.note: The transcript is posted in the Hall by supper, under the archive's plainest heading: 'Origins — answered as far as anyone honest can.' Someone underlines the child's verdict in pencil. Over the following weeks, in the way of this town, the pencil line is joined by dozens more — until the truest sentence in the record is also, by common consent, the most decorated.
